hints: Look at each pair of $y$ against $t$ graphs and count how many complete cycles each wave makes between the same vertical dashed time markers.
Recall that coherent waves must have the same frequency $f$ and a constant phase difference, which means the same period $T$ on a $y$-$t$ plot and a fixed shift between the traces.
Check which pair has different periods and also check whether a constant time shift or an on-off amplitude pattern alone breaks the constant phase-difference rule.
walkthrough: Identify what the diagram shows: for each option there are two $y$-$t$ plots at a fixed point, so the time between successive peaks is the period $T$ and $f = 1/T$.
State the coherence rule: two waves are coherent if they have the same frequency and a phase difference that does not change with time.
Compare cycles: in A, B and D the upper and lower traces repeat with the same $T$, only shifted in time or interrupted in amplitude, so $f$ is the same and the shift stays fixed.
Compare cycles in C: the upper wave makes one full oscillation where the lower wave makes about two full oscillations between the same dashed lines, so $T$ is different and $f$ is different.
Different frequencies mean the phase difference must drift continuously, so the pair cannot produce a stable interference pattern. This is option C.

A.explanation: Both $y$-$t$ traces complete the same number of cycles in the same time, with a fixed shift between peaks, so frequency is the same and phase difference is constant.

B.explanation: Both traces have the same period and the second wave stays about half a cycle behind the first, so frequency is the same and phase difference is constant.

C.explanation: The lower trace completes about twice as many oscillations as the upper trace between the same dashed time markers, so the frequencies differ and the waves cannot be coherent.

D.explanation: Both traces have the same spacing of peaks when they are present, so they share the same frequency and maintain the same phase relationship.
